name: CMS Energy Corporation

profile.description: CMS Energy is a Michigan utility holding company whose principal subsidiary, Consumers Energy, provides regulated electric and natural gas service across Michigan; NorthStar Clean Energy holds its non-utility generation business. Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.44 (vs $1.23 consensus) while GAAP EPS fell to $0.39 on NorthStar impairment and restructuring charges; 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.83–3.90 (targeting the high end), 2027 guidance of $4.08–4.17 and 6–8% long-term growth were reaffirmed [1]. Consumers has a signed 1 GW hyperscale data-center agreement within a ~9 GW pipeline [4]. CEO Garrick Rochow has led since 2020.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): CMS is executing a long-running clean-energy transition of its generation fleet and restructuring NorthStar Clean Energy, but a regulated utility's fleet transition is an industry-wide evolution rather than a new revenue stream, and Q3 2026 brought NorthStar impairments [1][5]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI savings were found [4]. Market Share (1/2): Consumers Energy holds a regulated franchise across much of Michigan — a protected position rather than share leadership [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Specific growth pipeline: a signed 1 GW hyperscale data-center contract, a ~9 GW data-center pipeline with load ramping toward 2029–2030 and the early 2030s, a $443M electric rate case with an order expected by April 2027, and 2027 EPS guidance of $4.08–4.17 [1][4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No meaningful R&D spending [3].
innovation.label: DEVELOPING

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): CMS frames its purpose around a 'triple bottom line' of people, planet and prosperity and 'world class performance delivering hometown service' — clear and Michigan-specific, but not transformative [5]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific charitable program with dollar amounts was identified in this research; a University of Michigan Ford School report criticized its political spending and executive pay [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of net insider buying in the last 12 months.
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on Dividend metrics (12 weight units): weighted sum 9.24 / 12 → 8. Forward P/E of 17.1 maxes out, as do 20 consecutive years of dividends since the 2007 reinstatement (2x) and 19 consecutive years of increases [2]. The 5-year dividend CAGR of 5.9% ($1.632 in 2020 to $2.172 in 2025) scores 0.98 on its 2x weight [2]. Revenue growth of 8% scores 0.93 and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 5.9% (derived from FMP: $6.42B in 2020 to $8.54B in 2025) scores 0.73 [3]. D/E of 196% scores 0.45, profit margin of 9.7% scores 0.49 and ROE of 5.3% scores 0.35 — both depressed by Q3 NorthStar impairments — and the GAAP payout ratio of 80% scores 0.33 [1][2]. Liquidity: ~3.85M shares/day × $70.76 ≈ $272M daily dollar volume [2].
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Generating and delivering electricity and gas over regulated physical networks cannot be displaced by AI, and AI is a direct demand tailwind — Consumers signed a 1 GW hyperscale data-center agreement and cites a ~9 GW pipeline, with load ramping toward the end of the decade [1][4]. It scores 8 rather than 9 because data-center load is not yet in the capital plan, and local zoning moratoriums are stalling several sites [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No direct AI revenue; data-center load is an indirect benefit not yet in rates.
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: CMS behaves like a long-horizon steward: a multi-decade dividend growth record since 2007, a generation-fleet transition planned over decades, and leadership drawn from within the company. Its purpose is genuine but bounded by the regulated utility model, and recent NorthStar impairments show that not every long-term bet has worked.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The 'people, planet, prosperity' triple bottom line and hometown-service commitment shape capital planning and the clean-energy transition across leadership changes [5]. It is not a 3 because the cause is largely shaped by regulation and has not been proven as a competitive advantage.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management took impairment and restructuring charges at NorthStar Clean Energy in Q3 2026, accepting a GAAP EPS drop to $0.39 rather than carrying underperforming non-utility assets, and is refusing to add data-center capex to its plan until siting conditions are met [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong — CEO Rochow is a long-time company insider — and the regulated workforce is stable, but no retention or engagement data supports a higher score [4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): CMS is reshaping its generation mix and adding large data-center load tariffs, an incremental adaptation within the regulated utility model [1][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence was found of management framing peer utilities as rivals to learn from; as a franchise monopoly it has limited direct competition.

investment_thesis: CMS is a premium regulated utility with visible growth: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.44 beat the $1.23 consensus, 2026 guidance of $3.83–3.90 (targeting the high end) and 2027 guidance of $4.08–4.17 were reaffirmed, and long-term 6–8% EPS growth is supported by rate-base investment [1]. A 1 GW hyperscale data-center contract and ~9 GW pipeline offer upside not yet in the capital plan [1][4]. The 3.22% yield has grown for 19 straight years, at a 5.9% 5-year CAGR, and the stock trades at 17.1x forward earnings [2]. The gas rate case was approved with a 9.8% ROE [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is regulatory and balance-sheet risk. The gas rate order granted only ~60% of the request ($139M), and the $443M electric case (10.25% ROE requested) is not decided until April 2027 [1]. D/E of 196% makes earnings sensitive to rates, and GAAP ROE of 5.3% and margin of 9.7% were hit by NorthStar impairments, lifting the GAAP payout ratio to 80% [2]. Data-center load is delayed by local zoning moratoriums, and a Yahoo PEG of 2.53 leaves limited valuation upside [1][2]. Inspire Impact Score of 53 (ALIGNED).
key_catalysts: Signing and siting the 1 GW hyperscale data center and adding data-center load from the ~9 GW pipeline to the capital plan after the midterm elections [1][4]
Michigan PSC electric rate order (requested $443M at a 10.25% ROE) expected by early April 2027 [1]
Delivering 2026 adjusted EPS at the high end of $3.83–3.90 and resetting NorthStar after the Q3 impairments [1]
key_risks: Adverse Michigan PSC rate outcomes — the gas case awarded ~60% of the request — limiting recovery of a large capital plan [1]
Data-center projects stalled by local zoning moratoriums and political opposition, delaying load growth [1][4]
High leverage (D/E 196%) and interest-rate sensitivity, with further NorthStar write-downs possible [1][2]
